content.thinking:
I'm tracing the incident: metrics stopped at 12:34, right after the deploy at 12:34:18 renamed the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`. The scrape config at c3c36da still selects `metrics`, while the values file at that commit uses `http-metrics`, so the mismatch is visible in what actually ran, not just in the planned changes.

I'm checking that the root cause rests on the scrape config and values files at the running revision, which show the mismatch directly. Next I'm comparing the error logs before and after the deploy, and they look about the same in rate, so serving didn't change. Last, I'm working out how to phrase the symptom: shoppers saw nothing wrong, and only the metrics stopped arriving.

I'm now setting out the causal chain: the shop's metrics stopped arriving from the onset minute while nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. The likely mechanism is that the scrape selector still names the old port, so there was nothing for it to pick up after the rename.

I'm now looking at why Prometheus stopped getting data: the scrape config at this revision selects a port named `metrics`, but no port on the service carries that name any more, so there's nothing to scrape. Next I'm tracing why that name went missing, which points at the deploy that renamed the port to `http-metrics`, and I'm checking whether an earlier deploy could explain it too.

I'm checking the earlier deploy as a candidate too: metrics were still arriving through minute 12:33 with that change in place, so it doesn't explain the gap. Nothing in the flag history changed in the hour before, so flags are ruled out as well.

I'm settling the causal chain now: the scrape selector names a port that no longer exists after the deploy's rename, so Prometheus has no target to scrape. The root cause is that the rename went into the values file while the scrape config still selects the old name `metrics`, and a name that matches no port silently yields an empty target list rather than an error.

I'm settling on the wording for the final write-up: the root cause is a port rename that left the scrape selector pointing at a name that no longer exists, so the fix still needs to put those names back into agreement. The remaining risk is that the shop's metrics keep failing to arrive, which would leave a real fault there unseen by any alert that reads them.

I'm now deciding how to record the contributing factor: nothing checks that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects matches the one the values file sets, and a mismatch yields an empty target list instead of an error. Had that check existed, the rename would have been caught before it went out, so the fix should add a check that covers every change like it.

I'm settling the second contributing factor now: the alert that fires on absent metrics didn't page anyone, so the gap ran on without a person looking at it. Paging someone would likely have shortened the incident, so I'm weighing that as a factor to record too.

I'm now considering whether the alert's late arrival also needs recording: the timing shows it came later than its evaluation window accounts for, and the record doesn't say what caused the rest of that delay, so I'll add an item to find out.

I'm turning to contributing factors now: the scrape selector never gets checked against the port name the values file sets, so a mismatch fails silently with an empty target list. Next I'm weighing whether the wider estate has the same drift, which means checking other services' scrape selectors for the old port names.

I'm now going through what went well in the response: the investigator traced the stop back to the deploy by reading the rollout state and diff, and Argus ruled out flag changes from the flag history. I'm also weighing whether declining to roll back the deliberate convention change, and leaving it to a person, belongs in that list, and I think the record supports it.

Next I'm deciding whether the missing page belongs in the contributing factors, since the alert routing was already in place before the incident. I'm also checking whether the went-well list needs anything beyond the investigator's rollout trace and the flag-history check, and I'm leaning toward leaving the other sections empty.

I'm assuming the deploy at 12:34:18 is what stopped the metrics, since it falls within the onset minute, and that the scrape and values files I read are what actually ran. I'm also taking the Service to have picked up its port names from the values file, and I'm working from logs alone, so any gap in measurement is unseen rather than recorded.

I'm now drafting the prevention item for the port mismatch: a check on deploy changes that fails when a ServiceMonitor names a port the Service doesn't declare. I'm also planning to audit other services touched by the estate-wide rename for scrape selectors still on the old names, and to route the absent-metrics alert for io-shop to on-call so someone is paged. Looking back at the ruled-out causes, the earlier deploy and the flag changes were both excluded by the metrics history and the flag history.

I'm pinning down the timing reference: I'll anchor the onset to the minute it started and avoid writing out clock times here. The deploy is the one that rolled the revision out, so I'm noting that every replica ran c3c36da by the time the rollout row was read, and I'll cite the supporting rows in the write-up.

action_items.item: Add a check to every change to deploy configuration, across all services, that fails when a ServiceMonitor endpoint names a port that the service's values file does not give any port.
Check the other services that the estate-wide port-naming convention renamed for ServiceMonitors that still select the old port names.
Route the MetricsAbsent alert for io-shop to the on-call rota so that it pages a person.
Find out what delayed the MetricsAbsent alert by {beyond_accounted_for} beyond what its evaluation interval and scraping allowance account for.

causal_chain.step: Nobody using the shop saw anything wrong. What was seen instead: the shop's metrics stopped arriving from the onset minute and had not come back.

Prometheus had no target to scrape. At the running revision, the shop's ServiceMonitor picks its scrape endpoint by the port name `metrics`, but the values file names the metrics port `http-metrics`. A name that matches no port gives an empty target list, not an error.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of revision 2c8f731. Metrics were still arriving with it in place, through the minute before the onset.
A feature-flag change. The flag provider's history showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour it read.

causal_chain.step: The port's name changed with the deploy of revision c3c36da at {P2.1}. That deploy renamed every port to the platform's `<protocol>[-<purpose>]` convention, including the metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics`. As of {T13.1}, every replica was running that revision.
The rename broke scraping because it changed only deploy/values-production.yaml and left deploy/scrape.yaml, which has to name the same port, still selecting `metrics`.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A planned renaming of the shop's network ports changed the name of the port the monitoring collects from, but the monitoring setup still looked for the old name, so it found nothing to collect.

contributing_factors.factor: No check was seen that the port name the ServiceMonitor selects matches the name the values file gives the metrics port. The scrape file itself says nothing checks that the two agree, and a mismatch gives an empty target list rather than an error.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check comparing the two names would have failed the renaming change before it went out, and the metrics would not have stopped.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The MetricsAbsent alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged on-call person could have taken up the escalation and the draft fix as soon as the alert fired, which would have shortened the time the shop went unmonitored.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read what the deployment of revision c3c36da changed, which showed the metrics port being renamed.
The Investigator Agent confirmed that every replica was running the deployed revision.
Argus read the flag provider's history and found no flag changes by anyone else.
Argus declined to undo the port rename, a deliberate change following the platform's naming convention, and left that decision to a person.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #571.

input.root_cause: The deploy renamed the shop's metrics port from `metrics` to `http-metrics` in deploy/values-production.yaml, but left deploy/scrape.yaml's ServiceMonitor selecting its scrape endpoint by the old name `metrics`. The ServiceMonitor finds that endpoint by port name, and a name that matches no port gives an empty target list rather than an error, so Prometheus had nothing to scrape.
input.still_at_risk: While the shop's metrics are not arriving, a real fault in the shop could go unnoticed by any alert that relies on those metrics.
input.symptom: No shopper saw anything wrong; the shop's metrics stopped arriving
